### **S7. Unpinned Dependency Versions (Supply Chain Risk) — MEDIUM**

```
Location: platformio.ini:29-30

WiFiManager and tinyxml2 are pulled from git HEAD without version 
pinning. A supply chain attack or breaking change would be pulled 
automatically.

Fix: Pin to specific commit hashes or tagged releases.
```

**Analysis Context:**
- This is a **medium-severity security finding** in the comprehensive codebase analysis
- Identified in the "Short-Term — Next Sprint (1-2 Weeks)" remediation roadmap as item #14
- The issue has already been discovered and documented by the project's code review process

---

### 5. **Dependency Pinning Strategy Summary**

| Approach | Libraries | Risk Level | Status |
|----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| **Caret-Pinned** | ArduinoJson, FastLED | Low-Medium | Safe: minor/patch updates only |
| **Unpinned (HEAD)** | WiFiManager, tinyxml2 | **High** | ⚠️ Vulnerable to breaking changes |

**Key Findings:**

1. **ArduinoJson & FastLED:** Using caret versioning (`^X.Y.Z`) provides reasonable protection by allowing only patch-level changes within a minor version
2. **WiFiManager & tinyxml2:** Pulling directly from git HEAD creates supply chain risk:
   - No protection against breaking API changes
   - No protection against malicious commits
   - Builds are non-deterministic across time
   - Previous attempt to pin to `^2.0.15-rc.1` was abandoned (line 28 is commented out)

---

Based on the S7 finding and best practices:

   - Example: `https://github.com/tzapu/WiFiManager.git@2.0.17`

2. **Immediate:** Pin tinyxml2 to a specific commit

   - Example: `https://github.com/leethomason/tinyxml2.git@<commit-hash>`

3. **Recommended:** Use semantic versioning for all git-based dependencies where tags exist

## JPL-MiniPulse Captive Portal & Web Server Code Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete findings:

---

### 1. **HTML Templates & Embedded HTML Strings**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3330-3362

Only **one custom HTML template** is embedded in the codebase:

```cpp
const char* update_button_html = R"---(
    <div>
        <div style="display: inline-block; border: 1px solid gray;padding:5px 20px;">
            <p id="firmwareStatus" style="margin-top:0;></p>
            <p id="updateResponse"></p>
            <button id="updateButton">Update Firmware</button>
        </div>
    </div>
    <script>
        fetch('/get-latest-version-number')
        .then(function (response) {
            return response.text();
        }).
        then(function (text) {
            document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").innerHTML = text;
            console.log(text);
        })

        document.getElementById("updateButton").addEventListener('click', function() {
            fetch('/trigger-firmware-update')
            .then(function (response) {
                return response.text();
            })
            .then(function (text) {
                document.getElementById("updateResponse").innerHTML = text;
                console.log("response:", text);
            })
            .catch(function (error) {
                console.error(error);
            });
        });
    </script>
)---";
```

This is injected into the WiFi portal as a custom head element via:
```cpp
wm.setCustomHeadElement(update_button_html);  // Line 3364
```

All other portal forms are **generated by WiFiManager library** (not custom HTML strings). The actual portal configuration form rendering is delegated to the WiFiManager library, which auto-generates HTML from the `WiFiManagerParameter` objects defined at lines 3310-3327.

---

### 2. **Web Server Route Handlers (Accepting User Input)**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 831-861 (webServerCallback function)

Three HTTP endpoints are registered:

#### **A. `/get-remote-version-number` (HTTP_GET)**
```cpp
wm.server->on("/get-remote-version-number", HTTP_GET, []() {
    const char* remoteFirmwareVersion = getRemoteFirmwareVersion();
    String response = "Remote Version: " + String(remoteFirmwareVersion);
    wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", response);
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters)
- **Action:** Fetches remote firmware version from `develop.kellerdigital.com`

#### **B. `/get-latest-version-number` (HTTP_GET)**
```cpp
wm.server->on("/get-latest-version-number", HTTP_GET, []() {
    const char* remoteFirmwareVersion = getRemoteFirmwareVersion();
    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
    const char* updateAvailableText = updateAvailable ? "true" : "false";
    String response = "Current version: " + String(currentFirmwareVersion) + 
                      "<br>Remote Version: " + String(remoteFirmwareVersion) + 
                      "<br>Update available: " + String(updateAvailableText);
    wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", response);
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters)
- **Action:** Returns version comparison info

#### **C. `/trigger-firmware-update` (HTTP_GET)** ⚠️ CRITICAL
```cpp
wm.server->on("/trigger-firmware-update", HTTP_GET, []() {
    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
    updateFirmwareOta();  // Initiates OTA update
    if (updateAvailable) {
        wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", "New firmware available, updating...");
    } else {
        wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", "Firmware is up to date");
    }
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters or body)
- **Action:** **Triggers firmware update immediately** with NO authentication
- **Vulnerability:** S2 (Unauthenticated OTA Trigger) — combined with S1 allows full device compromise

### **Portal Form Parameters (WiFiManager)**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3310-3327

Five configuration parameters are exposed via the WiFi portal:

| Parameter Name | Input Type | Min | Max | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | range slider | 8 | 160 | `param_brightness` | Maps 0-100 → 8-160 |
| `force-dummy-data` | range slider | 8 | 160 | `param_force_dummy_data` | ⚠️ Uses same range as brightness (bug) |
| `show_serial` | number | 0 | 1 | `param_show_serial` | Boolean flag |
| `show_diagnostics` | number | 0 | 1 | `param_show_diagnostics` | Boolean flag |
| `force_animation_type` | number | 0 | 5 | `param_force_animation_type` | 6 animation types |

The portal form is handled by the `saveParamsCallback()` function (lines 938-1042).

### 3. **Input Validation Analysis**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 938-1042 (saveParamsCallback)

**Critical Finding: NO SERVER-SIDE VALIDATION**

#### **Data Flow for Each Parameter:**

**A. Brightness (lines 995-1016)**
```cpp
String brightnessValue = getParam("brightness");          // Gets raw string
int brightnessInt = atoi(brightnessValue.c_str());        // ⚠️ atoi() - NO error checking
int brightnessMapped = MathHelpers::map(brightnessInt, 0, 100, 8, 160);
FileUtils::config.displayLED.brightness = brightnessInt;  // ⚠️ Stores unmapped value
FastLED.setBrightness(brightnessInt);                     // ⚠️ Uses unmapped value
```
- **Validation:** Client-side HTML `min='8' max='160'` ONLY
- **Issue:** `atoi()` returns 0 on parse failure (silent failure)
- **Issue:** The value is mapped but the unmapped value is stored in config
- **Issue:** Non-integer values silently convert to 0

**B. Show Serial (lines 943-960)**
```cpp
String showSerialValue = getParam("show_serial");
bool showSerialValueBool = strcmp(showSerialValue.c_str(), "1") == 0 ? true : false;
FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial = showSerialValueBool;
```
- **Validation:** String comparison to "1" (any other value = false)
- **Issue:** No validation that input is "0" or "1"

**C. Show Diagnostics (lines 965-980)**
```cpp
String showDiagnosticsValue = getParam("show_diagnostics");
bool showDiagnosticsValueBool = strcmp(showDiagnosticsValue.c_str(), "1") == 0 ? true : false;
FileUtils::config.debugUtils.diagMeasure = showDiagnosticsValueBool;
```
- **Validation:** Same as Show Serial (string comparison)
- **Issue:** No validation

**D. Force Animation Type (lines 985-991)**
```cpp
String forcedAnimationTypeValue = getParam("force_animation_type");
animate.forcedAnimationType = atoi(forcedAnimationTypeValue.c_str());
```
- **Validation:** Client-side HTML `min='0' max='5'` ONLY
- **Issue:** `atoi()` with no range validation (can exceed 5)
- **Issue:** No error checking if non-integer provided

**E. Force Dummy Data (lines 1021-1038)**
```cpp
String forceDummyDataInputValue = getParam("force_dummy_data");

**S5. Input Validation Weaknesses on Portal Parameters**

Specific lines cited:

- **Line 1005:** (unmapped brightness stored)
- **Line 1030:** `int forceDummyDataInt = atoi(forceDummyDataInputValue.c_str());`

**Recommended Fix:**

### 5. **Reference S10 - innerHTML Usage**

From `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/docs/codebase-analysis.md`, lines 383-389:

**S10. XSS via innerHTML in Portal JavaScript**

Two instances found in the custom HTML template (lines 3344 and 3354):

```javascript
// Line 3344: Firmware status display
document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").innerHTML = text;

// Line 3354: Update response display  
document.getElementById("updateResponse").innerHTML = text;
```

**Security Issue:**
> Custom portal HTML uses `innerHTML` to render server responses directly into the DOM. A MITM attacker on the HTTP firmware endpoint could inject JavaScript.

**Attack Vector:**
1. Device fetches version from `http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/latest_version.txt` (plain HTTP)
2. MITM attacker intercepts response
3. Attacker injects HTML/JavaScript payload
4. Browser executes injected code in portal context

**Recommended Fix:**
> Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`

**Corrected Code Should Be:**
```javascript
document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").textContent = text;
document.getElementById("updateResponse").textContent = text;
```

```text
     1→# JPL-MiniPulse Codebase Analysis
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-18
     4→**Firmware version analyzed:** 1.0.3
     5→**Branch:** `data/add-spacecraft`
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Table of Contents
    10→
    11→1. [Executive Summary](#executive-summary)
    12→2. [Architecture Analysis](#architecture-analysis)
    13→3. [Code Quality Findings](#code-quality-findings)
    14→4. [Security Assessment](#security-assessment)
    15→5. [Performance and Resource Analysis](#performance-and-resource-analysis)
    16→6. [Prioritized Remediation Roadmap](#prioritized-remediation-roadmap)
    17→
    18→---
    19→
    20→## Executive Summary
    21→
    22→JPL-MiniPulse is a well-conceived embedded system that fetches live NASA Deep Space Network telemetry and renders spacecraft communication data as LED animations across 2,565 WS2812B pixels on four concentric rings. The architecture leverages ESP32 dual-core FreeRTOS effectively, with a clean producer/consumer split between data acquisition (Core 0) and rendering (Core 1).
    23→
    24→**Quality Score: 6.5/10.** The system works and demonstrates strong domain understanding, but this analysis uncovered 4 critical bugs, 11 high-severity issues, and numerous medium-priority improvements across architecture, code quality, security, and performance.
    25→
    26→### Key Findings at a Glance
    27→
    28→| Category | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
    29→|----------|----------|------|--------|-----|
    30→| Code Quality / Bugs | 4 | 7 | 7 | - |
    31→| Security | 2 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
    32→| Performance | 1 | 4 | 6 | - |
    33→| Architecture | - | 3 | 4 | - |
    34→
    35→The most urgent issues are: a queue/task initialization race condition, `==` vs `=` bugs in semaphore tracking, a queue send type mismatch, OTA firmware updates over plain HTTP, and an unauthenticated firmware update trigger endpoint.
    36→
    37→---
    38→
    39→## Architecture Analysis
    40→
    41→### Overall Pattern: Dual-Core Producer-Consumer
    42→
    43→The system follows a classic producer-consumer pattern mediated by a FreeRTOS queue:
    44→
    45→```
    46→Core 0 (Producer)             FreeRTOS Queue            Core 1 (Consumer)
    47→getData() task       --->   xQueueCreate(5)    --->    loop() dequeues
    48→  fetchData()                                           updateAnimation()
    49→  parseData()                                           scrollLetters()
    50→  xQueueSend()                                          doRateBasedAnimation()
    51→                                                        drawMeteors()
    52→                                                        FastLED.show()
    53→```
    54→
    55→**Strengths:**
    56→- Clean separation of I/O-bound work (HTTP fetch, XML parse) from real-time rendering
    57→- Queue provides natural back-pressure (max 5 items)
    58→- Watchdog timer integration prevents hangs on either core
    59→
    60→**Weaknesses:**
    61→- No formal state machine governs lifecycle transitions. States are tracked via ~10 scattered boolean flags (`nameScrollDone`, `animationInProgress`, `animateFirstCycleDown`, `dataStarted`, `portalRunning`, `otaUpdateTriggered`, `usingDummyData`, etc.)
    62→
    63→### Module Organization
    64→
    65→| Module | Location | LOC | Responsibility | Coupling |
    66→|--------|----------|-----|----------------|----------|
    67→| **main** | `src/main.cpp` | ~3,650 | Everything else | Monolith |
    68→| **Animate** | `lib/Animate/` | ~220 | Meteor rendering engine | AnimationUtils, MathHelpers, FastLED |
    69→| **AnimationUtils** | `lib/AnimationUtils/` | ~130 | Color definitions, brightness | FileUtils, FastLED, MathHelpers |
    70→| **DevUtils** | `lib/DevUtils/` | ~180 | Serial formatting, ANSI colors | WiFiManager |
    71→| **FileUtils** | `lib/FileUtils/` | ~560 | LittleFS I/O, config management | ArduinoJson, LittleFS |
    72→| **MathHelpers** | `lib/MathHelpers/` | ~38 | Utility math | None (pure) |
    73→| **SpacecraftData** | `lib/SpacecraftData/` | ~910 | Name/blacklist/rate lookups | FileUtils, DevUtils, ArduinoJson |
    74→| **TextCharacters** | `lib/TextCharacters/` | ~1,780 | Bitmap font definitions | None (pure data) |
    75→
    76→### Architectural Issues
    77→
    78→#### A1. Monolithic main.cpp (~3,650 lines) — HIGH
    79→
    80→`src/main.cpp` contains animation orchestration, data fetching, HTTP handling, XML parsing, WiFi management, OTA updates, queue management, semaphore pool management, serial debugging, and the main loop. At minimum these should be extracted:
    81→- `DataFetcher` — `fetchData`, `fetchHTTPData`, `generateFetchUrl`, `handleHttpResponse`
    82→- `DataParser` — `parseData`, `findSignals`, `rateLongToRateClass`
    83→- `AnimationController` — `doRateBasedAnimation`, `createMeteor`, all animation patterns
    84→- `WiFiController` — `doWiFiManager`, `webServerCallback`, `saveParamsCallback`
    85→- `OTAUpdater` — `setupOtaUpdate`, `updateFirmwareOta`, `checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable`
    86→
    87→#### A2. Configuration Duplication — HIGH
    88→
    89→Compile-time constants in `main.cpp` (lines 350-415) duplicate runtime config values in `FileUtils::config`. For example, `outerPixelsTotal = 800` at `main.cpp:377` duplicates `config.displayLED.outerPixelsTotal = 800` at `FileUtils.cpp:31`. The compile-time constants are actually used for LED array sizing and runtime loops, while many config values go unused. This creates confusion about source of truth.
    90→
    91→Additionally, `setConfigValuesFromFile()` (`FileUtils.cpp:287-314`) only reads 3 keys (`showSerial`, `diagMeasure`, `brightness`) from the JSON config file, even though the Config struct has dozens of fields.
    92→
    93→#### A3. SpacecraftData Redundant Write-Then-Read Cycle — HIGH
    94→
    95→`loadSpacecraftNamesFile()` (`SpacecraftData.cpp:155`) calls `createAndWriteNamesFile()` which populates the in-memory JSON document AND writes it to a file, then immediately reads the file back and deserializes it again. The data is already in memory after the write. Same pattern repeats for blacklist and placeholder rates. This doubles boot I/O and flash wear.
    96→
    97→#### A4. Coupling Issues — MEDIUM
    98→
    99→- `AnimationUtils` includes `FileUtils` for brightness access — a pure animation utility should not need filesystem access
   100→- `DevUtils` depends on `WiFiManager` just for the `printWiFiConfigBanner()` signature
   101→- `SpacecraftData` includes `FastLED` but never uses it directly
   102→- Forward declaration workaround in `FileUtils.h:33` (`class DevUtils;`) suggests a past circular dependency that was worked around rather than resolved
   103→
   104→#### A5. Commented-Out Code Debris — MEDIUM
   105→
   106→~500+ lines of dead commented-out code across the codebase:
   107→- `SpacecraftData.h:67-124` — entire duplicate class definition
   108→- `SpacecraftData.cpp:734-907` — hundreds of lines of PROGMEM implementations
   109→- `main.cpp:278-344` — WiFi parameter code
   110→
   111→All of this is preserved in git history and should be removed.
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→## Code Quality Findings
   116→
   117→### Critical Bugs
   118→
   119→#### CQ1. Task Created Before Queue Exists — CRITICAL
   120→
   121→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3495-3504`
   122→
   123→The `getData` task is pinned to Core 0 at line 3495 before the queue is created at line 3504. The task's `getData()` function references `queue` on line 3169 (`uxQueueSpacesAvailable(queue)`). If the task wakes up before `queue = xQueueCreate(...)` executes on Core 1, it will call FreeRTOS queue functions on a NULL handle, causing a crash or undefined behavior.
   124→
   125→```cpp
   126→// Line 3495 — task created BEFORE queue exists
   127→xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(getData, "getData", 6144, NULL, 0, &xHandleData, 0);
   128→
   129→// Line 3504 — queue created AFTER
   130→queue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem));
   131→```
   132→
   133→**Fix:** Create the queue before creating the task.
   134→
   135→#### CQ2. Semaphore Assignment Bug: `==` Instead of `=` — CRITICAL
   136→
   137→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2746, 2767`
   138→
   139→Two code paths use the comparison operator `==` where assignment `=` is required. `semaphoreTaken` is never set to `false`, meaning on the next call to `parseData()` the function may attempt to give a mutex that is already released.
   140→
   141→```cpp
   142→// Line 2746 — comparison, not assignment
   143→semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG: should be semaphoreTaken = false;
   144→```
   145→
   146→**Fix:** Change `==` to `=` at both locations.
   147→
   148→#### CQ3. Queue Sends Pointer-to-Pointer Instead of Struct — CRITICAL
   149→
   150→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2200, 3558`
   151→
   152→`xQueueSend` is called with `&newCraft` where `newCraft` is a `CraftQueueItem*`. This sends the address of the pointer (4 bytes of meaningful data) into a queue slot sized for the full struct (156 bytes). The receive side has the same mismatch.
   153→
   154→```cpp
   155→// Line 2200 — sends CraftQueueItem** instead of the struct
   156→if (xQueueSend(queue, &newCraft, 100) == pdPASS) {
   157→```
   158→
   159→**Fix:** Send the struct by value: `xQueueSend(queue, newCraft, 100)`.
   160→
   161→#### CQ4. assignValuesToCraftSemaphore Always Reads freeList[freeListTop] — CRITICAL
   162→
   163→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2257-2286`
   164→
   165→The loop iterates `i` from `MAX_ITEMS - 1` down to `1`, checks `freeList[i] != nullptr`, but then always reads from `freeList[freeListTop]` instead of `freeList[i]`. This may pick a null or wrong pool item.
   166→
   167→```cpp
   168→for (uint8_t i = MAX_ITEMS - 1; i > 0; i--) {
   169→    if (freeList[i] != nullptr) {
   170→        newCraft = freeList[freeListTop]; // BUG: should be freeList[i]
   171→        ...
   172→    }
   173→}
   174→```
   175→
   176→### High-Severity Issues
   177→
   178→#### CQ5. `isWiFiConnected` Missing Parentheses — Function Pointer Always Truthy
   179→
   180→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3120`
   181→
   182→```cpp
   183→if (!isWiFiConnected && wm.getWiFiIsSaved() == true) {
   184→```
   185→
   186→`isWiFiConnected` is a function. Without `()`, this evaluates the function's address (always non-null, always truthy), so `!isWiFiConnected` is always `false`. **The WiFi auto-reconnect logic never executes.**
   187→
   188→#### CQ6. `randomTypeAny` Uninitialized for Rate Classes 1 and 2
   189→
   190→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1665-1682`
   191→
   192→When `animateFirstCycleDown/Up` is true and `rateClass` is 1 or 2, the `if/else if` chain falls through without assigning `randomTypeAny`. The uninitialized value is used as an array index, causing out-of-bounds access.
   193→
   194→**Fix:** Initialize `uint8_t randomTypeAny = 0;`.
   195→
   196→#### CQ7. `freeSemaphoreItem` Nulls Local Copy, Not Caller's Pointer
   197→
   198→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:748-783`
   199→
   200→`infoBuffer = nullptr` at line 777 only nulls the local parameter copy. The caller retains a dangling pointer to a pool item that has been returned, enabling use-after-free if the item is immediately reused.
   201→
   202→#### CQ8. `delay()` Inside FreeRTOS Context
   203→
   204→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1484, 1492`
   205→
   206→`laserGunAnimation()` uses `delay()` which blocks Core 1 entirely without yielding to the FreeRTOS scheduler, potentially triggering the watchdog.
   207→
   208→**Fix:** Replace with `vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(...))`.
   209→
   210→#### CQ9. Global `colorTheme` Constant Shadows Parameter
   211→
   212→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:276, 868, 3478`
   213→
   214→A global `const uint8_t colorTheme = 0` is declared at line 276. At line 3478, `setColorTheme(colorTheme)` passes this constant value of 0, meaning the color theme can never be changed from the portal config. Should use `FileUtils::config.miscellaneous.colorTheme` instead.
   215→
   216→#### CQ10. `firstStartupAnimation` Logic Inverted
   217→
   218→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3599-3603`
   219→
   220→```cpp
   221→if (!firstStartupAnimation) {
   222→    firstStartupAnimation = false;  // already false — no-op
   223→} else {
   224→    displayDurationTimer = currentMillis;
   225→}
   226→```
   227→
   228→The flag is never set to `false`, meaning `displayDurationTimer` is reset on every new craft. The branches appear swapped.
   229→
   230→#### CQ11. `strncpy` Without Null-Termination Guarantee
   231→
   232→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:367-370`
   233→
   234→`strncpy` does not guarantee null-termination if the source fills the buffer. The fields `apSSID[32]`, `apPass[32]`, and `serverName[128]` are used as C-strings throughout. If a value exactly fills the buffer, string operations will read past the end.
   235→
   236→**Fix:** Add explicit null-termination after each `strncpy`, or use `strlcpy`.
   237→
   238→### Medium-Severity Issues
   239→
   240→#### CQ12. `LittleFS.begin()` Called Twice at Setup
   241→
   242→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3212-3219`
   243→
   244→Both calls pass `true` (format-if-failed). The second call is redundant and potentially re-formats the filesystem.
   245→
   246→#### CQ13. `printCurrentQueue` Drops Items on Failure
   247→
   248→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:664-703`
   249→
   250→Creates a temp queue, drains the real queue, and refills it. If `xQueueSend` to the temp queue fails mid-loop, items already dequeued are silently lost. Called on every queue receive when `showSerial` is true.
   251→
   252→#### CQ14. `snprintf` Missing Reset Color in Output
   253→
   254→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1692-1703`
   255→
   256→The format string has 4 specifiers but 5 arguments are passed. The reset color escape code is dropped, leaving the terminal stuck in cyan.
   257→
   258→#### CQ15. `retrieveQueueBuffer` Built but Never Printed
   259→
   260→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3561-3570`
   261→
   262→A formatted header string is populated via `snprintf` but `Serial.print()` is never called on it.
   263→
   264→#### CQ16. `handleException()` Is a No-Op
   265→
   266→**Location:** `lib/DevUtils/DevUtils.cpp:74-108`
   267→
   268→The entire exception handling body is commented out. Every catch block that calls `dev.handleException()` effectively silences the error with a generic message.
   269→
   270→#### CQ17. Uninitialized `characterTotalPixels` in `getCharacter()`
   271→
   272→**Location:** `lib/TextCharacters/TextCharacters.cpp:1756-1778`
   273→
   274→If `width` is not 3, 4, or 5, `characterTotalPixels` is uninitialized. The switch statement lacks a `default` case.
   275→
   276→#### CQ18. Config File Handle Leak on Deserialization Failure
   277→
   278→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:247-257`
   279→
   280→If `deserializeJson` fails in `setConfigValuesFromFile()`, the function returns without closing the file, relying on the File destructor.
   281→
   282→---
   283→
   284→## Security Assessment
   285→
   286→**Overall Risk Level: HIGH**
   287→
   288→While the device handles no sensitive user data, it has significant security weaknesses that could allow an attacker to fully compromise the device.
   289→
   290→### Critical Security Findings
   291→
   292→#### S1. OTA Firmware Update Over Unencrypted HTTP — CRITICAL
   293→
   294→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:451, 503`
   295→
   296→Both the version check and firmware binary download use plain HTTP to `develop.kellerdigital.com`. There is no TLS, no firmware signing, no hash verification, and no certificate pinning.
   297→
   298→```cpp
   299→httpFirmware.begin("http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/latest_version.txt");
   300→httpUpdate.update(client, "http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/firmware.bin");
   301→```
   302→
   303→**Impact:** Any attacker on the same network can MITM and serve arbitrary firmware, gaining complete control of the device. This can be used to exfiltrate WiFi credentials, brick the device, or use it as a network pivot.
   304→
   305→**Fix:** Switch to HTTPS with `WiFiClientSecure` and certificate validation. Implement firmware signing.
   306→
   307→#### S2. Unauthenticated OTA Trigger Endpoint — CRITICAL
   308→
   309→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:857-865`
   310→
   311→The WiFi portal exposes `GET /trigger-firmware-update` with no authentication.
   312→
   313→```cpp
   314→wm.server->on("/trigger-firmware-update", HTTP_GET, []() {
   315→    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
   316→    updateFirmwareOta();
   317→    ...
   318→});
   319→```
   320→
   321→**Impact:** Combined with S1, an attacker can both trigger the OTA process AND serve malicious firmware. A single `curl` command is sufficient.
   322→
   323→**Fix:** Require authentication, change to POST, add rate limiting, or require physical button press.
   324→
   325→### High-Severity Security Findings
   326→
   327→#### S3. Open WiFi Access Point With No Password
   328→
   329→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:14-15`
   330→
   331→The config AP password is set to an empty string, creating an open network anyone can join.
   332→
   333→**Fix:** Set a default WPA2 password.
   334→
   335→#### S4. No CSRF Protection on Portal Forms
   336→
   337→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:943-1047`
   338→
   339→The `saveParamsCallback` processes form submissions without CSRF token validation. Any client on the network can forge configuration changes.
   340→
   341→#### S5. Input Validation Weaknesses on Portal Parameters
   342→
   343→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:995, 1005, 1030`
   344→
   345→Portal values are converted via `atoi()` with no range validation before being applied to config.
   346→
   347→**Fix:** Use `strtol()` with error checking and clamp values server-side.
   348→
   349→#### S6. DSN Data Fetch May Lack TLS Verification
   350→
   351→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:16; src/main.cpp:2866`
   352→
   353→The DSN URL uses HTTPS but `HTTPClient` is initialized as a plain `HTTPClient` without `WiFiClientSecure`. The TLS handshake may proceed without certificate verification or may silently fail.
   354→
   355→**Fix:** Explicitly use `WiFiClientSecure` with root CA certificate for `eyes.nasa.gov`.
   356→
   357→### Medium-Severity Security Findings
   358→
   359→#### S7. Unpinned Dependency Versions (Supply Chain Risk)
   360→
   361→**Location:** `platformio.ini:29-30`
   362→
   363→WiFiManager and tinyxml2 are pulled from git HEAD without version pinning. A supply chain attack or breaking change would be pulled automatically.
   364→
   365→**Fix:** Pin to specific commit hashes or tagged releases.
   366→
   367→#### S8. Hardcoded Developer Infrastructure URL
   368→
   369→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:451, 503`
   370→
   371→OTA server is hardcoded to `develop.kellerdigital.com` — a development subdomain. If the domain registration lapses, an attacker could register it and serve malicious firmware to all deployed devices.
   372→
   373→**Fix:** Use a dedicated production domain; make OTA URL configurable.
   374→
   375→#### S9. Verbose Serial Output Exposes Operational Data
   376→
   377→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3208, 3238, 3458-3459`
   378→
   379→Several lines unconditionally output firmware version, DSN server URL, WiFi credential status, and the AP password to serial, regardless of the `showSerial` flag.
   380→
   381→**Fix:** Gate all serial output behind `showSerial`.
   382→
   383→#### S10. XSS via innerHTML in Portal JavaScript
   384→
   385→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3366, 3376`
   386→
   387→Custom portal HTML uses `innerHTML` to render server responses directly into the DOM. A MITM attacker on the HTTP firmware endpoint could inject JavaScript.
   388→
   389→**Fix:** Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`.
   390→
   391→#### S11. `fetchUrl` Buffer Fragility
   392→
   393→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2824-2839`
   394→
   395→The `fetchUrl` buffer is 64 bytes but `serverName` in config allows up to 128 bytes. If the server URL is changed to something longer, the URL would be silently truncated.
   396→
   397→**Fix:** Increase buffer to 192 bytes or validate `serverName` length on config load.
   398→
   399→### Full Attack Scenario
   400→
   401→1. Attacker approaches within WiFi range
   402→2. Connects to open "JPL MiniPulse" AP (no password — S3)
   403→3. Navigates to `http://192.168.4.1/trigger-firmware-update` (no auth — S2)
   404→4. Simultaneously performs ARP spoofing to intercept traffic to `develop.kellerdigital.com`
   405→5. Serves malicious firmware binary over plain HTTP (S1)
   406→6. Device flashes attacker's firmware — **full compromise**
   407→

   409→
   410→## Performance and Resource Analysis
   411→
   412→### Memory Budget
   413→
   414→| Component | Size | Type |
   415→|-----------|------|------|
   416→| LED pixel arrays (4 strips) | ~7.7 KB | Static |
   417→| FastLED RMT double-buffer | ~7.7 KB | Static (internal) |
   418→| `xmlDataBuffer[20480]` | 20 KB | Static local |
   419→| SpacecraftData JSON documents | ~12.3 KB | Heap (permanent) |
   420→| FreeRTOS queue (5 items) | ~780 B | Heap |
   421→| CraftQueueItem pool (5 items) | ~780 B | Static |
   422→| ActiveMeteors pointer array | 2 KB | Static |
   423→| Peak Meteor objects (up to 500) | up to ~36 KB | Heap (dynamic) |
   424→| WiFiManager + HTTP overhead | ~15-25 KB | Heap |
   425→| TinyXML2 parse tree (temporary) | ~5-15 KB | Heap (during parse) |
   426→| **Total peak estimate** | **~107-130 KB** | |
   427→
   428→ESP32 has ~320 KB SRAM total, with IDF overhead consuming ~100-130 KB. This leaves ~190-220 KB available. At peak meteor count, the system operates with **~60-110 KB of free heap** — workable but with limited margin, especially given heap fragmentation from `new`/`delete` Meteor churn.
   429→
   430→### LED Rendering Performance
   431→
   432→`FastLED.show()` at `main.cpp:2025` uses the WS2812B protocol across all 4 strips. With ESP32 RMT outputting in parallel, the blocking time equals the longest strip:
   433→
   434→```
   435→960 LEDs * 24 bits * 1.25us/bit = ~28.8ms (inner ring)
   436→```
   437→
   438→This gives a hard ceiling of **~34 FPS maximum**. The target of 60 FPS (`fpsRate = 60` at line 352) is unachievable. The `fpsInMs = 1000 / fpsRate` value computed at line 531 is **never used as a frame limiter** — `FastLED.show()` is called unconditionally on every loop iteration.
   439→
   440→### Critical Performance Issues
   441→
   442→#### P1. Meteor Heap Fragmentation — HIGH
   443→
   444→Each animation cycle creates multiple `Meteor` objects via `new` (`main.cpp:1241`) and deletes them via `delete` (`main.cpp:1903`). With up to 500 slots and animations repeating every ~3 seconds, this creates continuous heap fragmentation. Over hours/days of runtime, this can lead to allocation failures.
   445→
   446→**Fix:** Implement a fixed-size Meteor pool allocator.
   447→
   448→#### P2. LittleFS Double Write-Read Per Data Cycle — HIGH
   449→
   450→In `fetchHTTPData()`, the HTTP response is written to `/temp.xml` on LittleFS, then immediately read back into `xmlDataBuffer` in `fetchData()`. The `String res` already holds the data in RAM. This doubles I/O per cycle and accumulates flash wear (~8,640 write/delete cycles per day).
   451→
   452→**Fix:** Pass the HTTP response string directly to `parseData()` instead of routing through the filesystem.
   453→
   454→#### P3. No Frame Rate Limiter — HIGH
   455→
   456→`updateAnimation()` is called on every `loop()` iteration with no delay or frame-rate gate. `FastLED.show()` is called unconditionally, transmitting all pixel data even when nothing visually meaningful has changed since the last frame. This wastes CPU and could be capped at the achievable ~30 FPS.
   457→
   458→**Fix:** Add `EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(33)` around the render path, and `vTaskDelay(1)` when skipping frames.
   459→
   460→#### P4. `DevUtils::termColor()` Uses `std::map` with Heap Allocation — HIGH
   461→
   462→`DevUtils.cpp:4-55` uses a `static std::map<std::string, const char*>` for ANSI escape code lookup. Every call constructs a temporary `std::string` on the heap for the key lookup. This runs dozens of times per parse cycle when serial output is enabled.
   463→
   464→**Fix:** Replace with a simple switch statement or lookup array returning `const char*`.
   465→
   466→#### P5. Semaphore Held for ~1 Second During Parse — MEDIUM
   467→
   468→`parseData()` holds `freeListMutex` for the entire parse duration (~900-1000ms including `vTaskDelay(100)` calls at each loop iteration). `freeSemaphoreItem()` on Core 1 waits only 500ms. If the mutex is held longer, item return fails silently.
   469→
   470→**Fix:** Reduce critical section scope — only hold the mutex during pool allocation/deallocation, not during the full parse.
   471→
   472→#### P6. WiFi Always-On Dual Mode — MEDIUM
   473→
   474→WiFi runs in `WIFI_AP_STA` mode permanently, keeping both station and soft AP active. The AP consumes ~50-100mA continuously even when no clients are connected.
   475→
   476→**Fix:** After initial configuration, switch to `WIFI_STA` mode.
   477→
   478→#### P7. Boot Time: ~15-20 Seconds — MEDIUM
   479→
   480→Two `delay(1000)` calls contribute 2 seconds; WiFi connection takes 3-10 seconds; SpacecraftData unconditionally writes all 3 JSON files to flash on every boot (even though the data is hardcoded and cannot change between boots). Adding a version check could skip the writes on normal boots.
   481→
   482→#### P8. Double Pass Over 500-Slot Meteor Array Per Frame — MEDIUM
   483→
   484→Every frame iterates the full `ActiveMeteors[500]` array twice: once in `drawMeteors()` and once in `updateMeteors()`. When only 10 meteors are active, 98% of iterations are null-pointer checks. A packed array with an active count would eliminate this waste.
   485→
   486→#### P9. XML Parse Traversal Overhead — MEDIUM
   487→
   488→The counter-based position tracking system (`stationCount`, `dishCount`, `targetCount`) requires iterating through the full DOM to reach the desired position on each parse cycle. The outer loop at line 2396 (`for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)`) runs the entire parse logic twice as a retry, doubling parse time.
   489→
   490→#### P10. `logOutput()` Uses `malloc` Per Call — LOW
   491→
   492→The debug function allocates a dynamic buffer via `malloc` on every invocation. A fixed-size stack buffer would eliminate heap allocation in the logging path.
   493→
   494→---

```text
     1→# JPL-MiniPulse Codebase Analysis
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-18
     4→**Firmware version analyzed:** 1.0.3
     5→**Branch:** `data/add-spacecraft`
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Table of Contents
    10→
    11→1. [Executive Summary](#executive-summary)
    12→2. [Architecture Analysis](#architecture-analysis)
    13→3. [Code Quality Findings](#code-quality-findings)
    14→4. [Security Assessment](#security-assessment)
    15→5. [Performance and Resource Analysis](#performance-and-resource-analysis)
    16→6. [Prioritized Remediation Roadmap](#prioritized-remediation-roadmap)
    17→
    18→---
    19→
    20→## Executive Summary
    21→
    22→JPL-MiniPulse is a well-conceived embedded system that fetches live NASA Deep Space Network telemetry and renders spacecraft communication data as LED animations across 2,565 WS2812B pixels on four concentric rings. The architecture leverages ESP32 dual-core FreeRTOS effectively, with a clean producer/consumer split between data acquisition (Core 0) and rendering (Core 1).
    23→
    24→**Quality Score: 6.5/10.** The system works and demonstrates strong domain understanding, but this analysis uncovered 4 critical bugs, 11 high-severity issues, and numerous medium-priority improvements across architecture, code quality, security, and performance.
    25→
    26→### Key Findings at a Glance
    27→
    28→| Category | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
    29→|----------|----------|------|--------|-----|
    30→| Code Quality / Bugs | 4 | 7 | 7 | - |
    31→| Security | 2 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
    32→| Performance | 1 | 4 | 6 | - |
    33→| Architecture | - | 3 | 4 | - |
    34→
    35→The most urgent issues are: a queue/task initialization race condition, `==` vs `=` bugs in semaphore tracking, a queue send type mismatch, OTA firmware updates over plain HTTP, and an unauthenticated firmware update trigger endpoint.
    36→
    37→---
    38→
    39→## Architecture Analysis
    40→
    41→### Overall Pattern: Dual-Core Producer-Consumer
    42→
    43→The system follows a classic producer-consumer pattern mediated by a FreeRTOS queue:
    44→
    45→```
    46→Core 0 (Producer)             FreeRTOS Queue            Core 1 (Consumer)
    47→getData() task       --->   xQueueCreate(5)    --->    loop() dequeues
    48→  fetchData()                                           updateAnimation()
    49→  parseData()                                           scrollLetters()
    50→  xQueueSend()                                          doRateBasedAnimation()
    51→                                                        drawMeteors()
    52→                                                        FastLED.show()
    53→```
    54→
    55→**Strengths:**
    56→- Clean separation of I/O-bound work (HTTP fetch, XML parse) from real-time rendering
    57→- Queue provides natural back-pressure (max 5 items)
    58→- Watchdog timer integration prevents hangs on either core
    59→
    60→**Weaknesses:**
    61→- No formal state machine governs lifecycle transitions. States are tracked via ~10 scattered boolean flags (`nameScrollDone`, `animationInProgress`, `animateFirstCycleDown`, `dataStarted`, `portalRunning`, `otaUpdateTriggered`, `usingDummyData`, etc.)
    62→
    63→### Module Organization
    64→
    65→| Module | Location | LOC | Responsibility | Coupling |
    66→|--------|----------|-----|----------------|----------|
    67→| **main** | `src/main.cpp` | ~3,650 | Everything else | Monolith |
    68→| **Animate** | `lib/Animate/` | ~220 | Meteor rendering engine | AnimationUtils, MathHelpers, FastLED |
    69→| **AnimationUtils** | `lib/AnimationUtils/` | ~130 | Color definitions, brightness | FileUtils, FastLED, MathHelpers |
    70→| **DevUtils** | `lib/DevUtils/` | ~180 | Serial formatting, ANSI colors | WiFiManager |
    71→| **FileUtils** | `lib/FileUtils/` | ~560 | LittleFS I/O, config management | ArduinoJson, LittleFS |
    72→| **MathHelpers** | `lib/MathHelpers/` | ~38 | Utility math | None (pure) |
    73→| **SpacecraftData** | `lib/SpacecraftData/` | ~910 | Name/blacklist/rate lookups | FileUtils, DevUtils, ArduinoJson |
    74→| **TextCharacters** | `lib/TextCharacters/` | ~1,780 | Bitmap font definitions | None (pure data) |
    75→
    76→### Architectural Issues
    77→
    78→#### A1. Monolithic main.cpp (~3,650 lines) — HIGH
    79→
    80→`src/main.cpp` contains animation orchestration, data fetching, HTTP handling, XML parsing, WiFi management, OTA updates, queue management, semaphore pool management, serial debugging, and the main loop. At minimum these should be extracted:
    81→- `DataFetcher` — `fetchData`, `fetchHTTPData`, `generateFetchUrl`, `handleHttpResponse`
    82→- `DataParser` — `parseData`, `findSignals`, `rateLongToRateClass`
    83→- `AnimationController` — `doRateBasedAnimation`, `createMeteor`, all animation patterns
    84→- `WiFiController` — `doWiFiManager`, `webServerCallback`, `saveParamsCallback`
    85→- `OTAUpdater` — `setupOtaUpdate`, `updateFirmwareOta`, `checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable`
    86→
    87→#### A2. Configuration Duplication — HIGH
    88→
    89→Compile-time constants in `main.cpp` (lines 350-415) duplicate runtime config values in `FileUtils::config`. For example, `outerPixelsTotal = 800` at `main.cpp:377` duplicates `config.displayLED.outerPixelsTotal = 800` at `FileUtils.cpp:31`. The compile-time constants are actually used for LED array sizing and runtime loops, while many config values go unused. This creates confusion about source of truth.
    90→
    91→Additionally, `setConfigValuesFromFile()` (`FileUtils.cpp:287-314`) only reads 3 keys (`showSerial`, `diagMeasure`, `brightness`) from the JSON config file, even though the Config struct has dozens of fields.
    92→
    93→#### A3. SpacecraftData Redundant Write-Then-Read Cycle — HIGH
    94→
    95→`loadSpacecraftNamesFile()` (`SpacecraftData.cpp:155`) calls `createAndWriteNamesFile()` which populates the in-memory JSON document AND writes it to a file, then immediately reads the file back and deserializes it again. The data is already in memory after the write. Same pattern repeats for blacklist and placeholder rates. This doubles boot I/O and flash wear.
    96→
    97→#### A4. Coupling Issues — MEDIUM
    98→
    99→- `AnimationUtils` includes `FileUtils` for brightness access — a pure animation utility should not need filesystem access
   100→- `DevUtils` depends on `WiFiManager` just for the `printWiFiConfigBanner()` signature
   101→- `SpacecraftData` includes `FastLED` but never uses it directly
   102→- Forward declaration workaround in `FileUtils.h:33` (`class DevUtils;`) suggests a past circular dependency that was worked around rather than resolved
   103→
   104→#### A5. Commented-Out Code Debris — MEDIUM
   105→
   106→~500+ lines of dead commented-out code across the codebase:
   107→- `SpacecraftData.h:67-124` — entire duplicate class definition
   108→- `SpacecraftData.cpp:734-907` — hundreds of lines of PROGMEM implementations
   109→- `main.cpp:278-344` — WiFi parameter code
   110→
   111→All of this is preserved in git history and should be removed.
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→## Code Quality Findings
   116→
   117→### Critical Bugs
   118→
   119→#### CQ1. Task Created Before Queue Exists — CRITICAL
   120→
   121→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3495-3504`
   122→
   123→The `getData` task is pinned to Core 0 at line 3495 before the queue is created at line 3504. The task's `getData()` function references `queue` on line 3169 (`uxQueueSpacesAvailable(queue)`). If the task wakes up before `queue = xQueueCreate(...)` executes on Core 1, it will call FreeRTOS queue functions on a NULL handle, causing a crash or undefined behavior.
   124→
   125→```cpp
   126→// Line 3495 — task created BEFORE queue exists
   127→xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(getData, "getData", 6144, NULL, 0, &xHandleData, 0);
   128→
   129→// Line 3504 — queue created AFTER
   130→queue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem));
   131→```
   132→
   133→**Fix:** Create the queue before creating the task.
   134→
   135→#### CQ2. Semaphore Assignment Bug: `==` Instead of `=` — CRITICAL
   136→
   137→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2746, 2767`
   138→
   139→Two code paths use the comparison operator `==` where assignment `=` is required. `semaphoreTaken` is never set to `false`, meaning on the next call to `parseData()` the function may attempt to give a mutex that is already released.
   140→
   141→```cpp
   142→// Line 2746 — comparison, not assignment
   143→semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG: should be semaphoreTaken = false;
   144→```
   145→
   146→**Fix:** Change `==` to `=` at both locations.
   147→
   148→#### CQ3. Queue Sends Pointer-to-Pointer Instead of Struct — CRITICAL
   149→
   150→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2200, 3558`
   151→
   152→`xQueueSend` is called with `&newCraft` where `newCraft` is a `CraftQueueItem*`. This sends the address of the pointer (4 bytes of meaningful data) into a queue slot sized for the full struct (156 bytes). The receive side has the same mismatch.
   153→
   154→```cpp
   155→// Line 2200 — sends CraftQueueItem** instead of the struct
   156→if (xQueueSend(queue, &newCraft, 100) == pdPASS) {
   157→```
   158→
   159→**Fix:** Send the struct by value: `xQueueSend(queue, newCraft, 100)`.
   160→
   161→#### CQ4. assignValuesToCraftSemaphore Always Reads freeList[freeListTop] — CRITICAL
   162→
   163→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2257-2286`
   164→
   165→The loop iterates `i` from `MAX_ITEMS - 1` down to `1`, checks `freeList[i] != nullptr`, but then always reads from `freeList[freeListTop]` instead of `freeList[i]`. This may pick a null or wrong pool item.
   166→
   167→```cpp
   168→for (uint8_t i = MAX_ITEMS - 1; i > 0; i--) {
   169→    if (freeList[i] != nullptr) {
   170→        newCraft = freeList[freeListTop]; // BUG: should be freeList[i]
   171→        ...
   172→    }
   173→}
   174→```
   175→
   176→### High-Severity Issues
   177→
   178→#### CQ5. `isWiFiConnected` Missing Parentheses — Function Pointer Always Truthy
   179→
   180→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3120`
   181→
   182→```cpp
   183→if (!isWiFiConnected && wm.getWiFiIsSaved() == true) {
   184→```
   185→
   186→`isWiFiConnected` is a function. Without `()`, this evaluates the function's address (always non-null, always truthy), so `!isWiFiConnected` is always `false`. **The WiFi auto-reconnect logic never executes.**
   187→
   188→#### CQ6. `randomTypeAny` Uninitialized for Rate Classes 1 and 2
   189→
   190→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1665-1682`
   191→
   192→When `animateFirstCycleDown/Up` is true and `rateClass` is 1 or 2, the `if/else if` chain falls through without assigning `randomTypeAny`. The uninitialized value is used as an array index, causing out-of-bounds access.
   193→
   194→**Fix:** Initialize `uint8_t randomTypeAny = 0;`.
   195→
   196→#### CQ7. `freeSemaphoreItem` Nulls Local Copy, Not Caller's Pointer
   197→
   198→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:748-783`
   199→
   200→`infoBuffer = nullptr` at line 777 only nulls the local parameter copy. The caller retains a dangling pointer to a pool item that has been returned, enabling use-after-free if the item is immediately reused.
   201→
   202→#### CQ8. `delay()` Inside FreeRTOS Context
   203→
   204→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1484, 1492`
   205→
   206→`laserGunAnimation()` uses `delay()` which blocks Core 1 entirely without yielding to the FreeRTOS scheduler, potentially triggering the watchdog.
   207→
   208→**Fix:** Replace with `vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(...))`.
   209→
   210→#### CQ9. Global `colorTheme` Constant Shadows Parameter
   211→
   212→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:276, 868, 3478`
   213→
   214→A global `const uint8_t colorTheme = 0` is declared at line 276. At line 3478, `setColorTheme(colorTheme)` passes this constant value of 0, meaning the color theme can never be changed from the portal config. Should use `FileUtils::config.miscellaneous.colorTheme` instead.
   215→
   216→#### CQ10. `firstStartupAnimation` Logic Inverted
   217→
   218→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3599-3603`
   219→
   220→```cpp
   221→if (!firstStartupAnimation) {
   222→    firstStartupAnimation = false;  // already false — no-op
   223→} else {
   224→    displayDurationTimer = currentMillis;
   225→}
   226→```
   227→
   228→The flag is never set to `false`, meaning `displayDurationTimer` is reset on every new craft. The branches appear swapped.
   229→
   230→#### CQ11. `strncpy` Without Null-Termination Guarantee
   231→
   232→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:367-370`
   233→
   234→`strncpy` does not guarantee null-termination if the source fills the buffer. The fields `apSSID[32]`, `apPass[32]`, and `serverName[128]` are used as C-strings throughout. If a value exactly fills the buffer, string operations will read past the end.
   235→
   236→**Fix:** Add explicit null-termination after each `strncpy`, or use `strlcpy`.
   237→
   238→### Medium-Severity Issues
   239→
   240→#### CQ12. `LittleFS.begin()` Called Twice at Setup
   241→
   242→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3212-3219`
   243→
   244→Both calls pass `true` (format-if-failed). The second call is redundant and potentially re-formats the filesystem.
   245→
   246→#### CQ13. `printCurrentQueue` Drops Items on Failure
   247→
   248→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:664-703`
   249→
   250→Creates a temp queue, drains the real queue, and refills it. If `xQueueSend` to the temp queue fails mid-loop, items already dequeued are silently lost. Called on every queue receive when `showSerial` is true.
   251→
   252→#### CQ14. `snprintf` Missing Reset Color in Output
   253→
   254→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:1692-1703`
   255→
   256→The format string has 4 specifiers but 5 arguments are passed. The reset color escape code is dropped, leaving the terminal stuck in cyan.
   257→
   258→#### CQ15. `retrieveQueueBuffer` Built but Never Printed
   259→
   260→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3561-3570`
   261→
   262→A formatted header string is populated via `snprintf` but `Serial.print()` is never called on it.
   263→
   264→#### CQ16. `handleException()` Is a No-Op
   265→
   266→**Location:** `lib/DevUtils/DevUtils.cpp:74-108`
   267→
   268→The entire exception handling body is commented out. Every catch block that calls `dev.handleException()` effectively silences the error with a generic message.
   269→
   270→#### CQ17. Uninitialized `characterTotalPixels` in `getCharacter()`
   271→
   272→**Location:** `lib/TextCharacters/TextCharacters.cpp:1756-1778`
   273→
   274→If `width` is not 3, 4, or 5, `characterTotalPixels` is uninitialized. The switch statement lacks a `default` case.
   275→
   276→#### CQ18. Config File Handle Leak on Deserialization Failure
   277→
   278→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:247-257`
   279→
   280→If `deserializeJson` fails in `setConfigValuesFromFile()`, the function returns without closing the file, relying on the File destructor.
   281→
   282→---
   283→
   284→## Security Assessment
   285→
   286→**Overall Risk Level: HIGH**
   287→
   288→While the device handles no sensitive user data, it has significant security weaknesses that could allow an attacker to fully compromise the device.
   289→
   290→### Critical Security Findings
   291→
   292→#### S1. OTA Firmware Update Over Unencrypted HTTP — CRITICAL
   293→
   294→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:451, 503`
   295→
   296→Both the version check and firmware binary download use plain HTTP to `develop.kellerdigital.com`. There is no TLS, no firmware signing, no hash verification, and no certificate pinning.
   297→
   298→```cpp
   299→httpFirmware.begin("http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/latest_version.txt");
   300→httpUpdate.update(client, "http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/firmware.bin");
   301→```
   302→
   303→**Impact:** Any attacker on the same network can MITM and serve arbitrary firmware, gaining complete control of the device. This can be used to exfiltrate WiFi credentials, brick the device, or use it as a network pivot.
   304→
   305→**Fix:** Switch to HTTPS with `WiFiClientSecure` and certificate validation. Implement firmware signing.
   306→
   307→#### S2. Unauthenticated OTA Trigger Endpoint — CRITICAL
   308→
   309→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:857-865`
   310→
   311→The WiFi portal exposes `GET /trigger-firmware-update` with no authentication.
   312→
   313→```cpp
   314→wm.server->on("/trigger-firmware-update", HTTP_GET, []() {
   315→    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
   316→    updateFirmwareOta();
   317→    ...
   318→});
   319→```
   320→
   321→**Impact:** Combined with S1, an attacker can both trigger the OTA process AND serve malicious firmware. A single `curl` command is sufficient.
   322→
   323→**Fix:** Require authentication, change to POST, add rate limiting, or require physical button press.
   324→
   325→### High-Severity Security Findings
   326→
   327→#### S3. Open WiFi Access Point With No Password
   328→
   329→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:14-15`
   330→
   331→The config AP password is set to an empty string, creating an open network anyone can join.
   332→
   333→**Fix:** Set a default WPA2 password.
   334→
   335→#### S4. No CSRF Protection on Portal Forms
   336→
   337→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:943-1047`
   338→
   339→The `saveParamsCallback` processes form submissions without CSRF token validation. Any client on the network can forge configuration changes.
   340→
   341→#### S5. Input Validation Weaknesses on Portal Parameters
   342→
   343→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:995, 1005, 1030`
   344→
   345→Portal values are converted via `atoi()` with no range validation before being applied to config.
   346→
   347→**Fix:** Use `strtol()` with error checking and clamp values server-side.
   348→
   349→#### S6. DSN Data Fetch May Lack TLS Verification
   350→
   351→**Location:** `lib/FileUtils/FileUtils.cpp:16; src/main.cpp:2866`
   352→
   353→The DSN URL uses HTTPS but `HTTPClient` is initialized as a plain `HTTPClient` without `WiFiClientSecure`. The TLS handshake may proceed without certificate verification or may silently fail.
   354→
   355→**Fix:** Explicitly use `WiFiClientSecure` with root CA certificate for `eyes.nasa.gov`.
   356→
   357→### Medium-Severity Security Findings
   358→
   359→#### S7. Unpinned Dependency Versions (Supply Chain Risk)
   360→
   361→**Location:** `platformio.ini:29-30`
   362→
   363→WiFiManager and tinyxml2 are pulled from git HEAD without version pinning. A supply chain attack or breaking change would be pulled automatically.
   364→
   365→**Fix:** Pin to specific commit hashes or tagged releases.
   366→
   367→#### S8. Hardcoded Developer Infrastructure URL
   368→
   369→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:451, 503`
   370→
   371→OTA server is hardcoded to `develop.kellerdigital.com` — a development subdomain. If the domain registration lapses, an attacker could register it and serve malicious firmware to all deployed devices.
   372→
   373→**Fix:** Use a dedicated production domain; make OTA URL configurable.
   374→
   375→#### S9. Verbose Serial Output Exposes Operational Data
   376→
   377→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3208, 3238, 3458-3459`
   378→
   379→Several lines unconditionally output firmware version, DSN server URL, WiFi credential status, and the AP password to serial, regardless of the `showSerial` flag.
   380→
   381→**Fix:** Gate all serial output behind `showSerial`.
   382→
   383→#### S10. XSS via innerHTML in Portal JavaScript
   384→
   385→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:3366, 3376`
   386→
   387→Custom portal HTML uses `innerHTML` to render server responses directly into the DOM. A MITM attacker on the HTTP firmware endpoint could inject JavaScript.
   388→
   389→**Fix:** Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`.
   390→
   391→#### S11. `fetchUrl` Buffer Fragility
   392→
   393→**Location:** `src/main.cpp:2824-2839`
   394→
   395→The `fetchUrl` buffer is 64 bytes but `serverName` in config allows up to 128 bytes. If the server URL is changed to something longer, the URL would be silently truncated.
   396→
   397→**Fix:** Increase buffer to 192 bytes or validate `serverName` length on config load.
   398→
   399→### Full Attack Scenario
   400→
   401→1. Attacker approaches within WiFi range
   402→2. Connects to open "JPL MiniPulse" AP (no password — S3)
   403→3. Navigates to `http://192.168.4.1/trigger-firmware-update` (no auth — S2)
   404→4. Simultaneously performs ARP spoofing to intercept traffic to `develop.kellerdigital.com`
   405→5. Serves malicious firmware binary over plain HTTP (S1)
   406→6. Device flashes attacker's firmware — **full compromise**
   407→
   408→---
   409→
   410→## Performance and Resource Analysis
   411→
   412→### Memory Budget
   413→
   414→| Component | Size | Type |
   415→|-----------|------|------|
   416→| LED pixel arrays (4 strips) | ~7.7 KB | Static |
   417→| FastLED RMT double-buffer | ~7.7 KB | Static (internal) |
   418→| `xmlDataBuffer[20480]` | 20 KB | Static local |
   419→| SpacecraftData JSON documents | ~12.3 KB | Heap (permanent) |
   420→| FreeRTOS queue (5 items) | ~780 B | Heap |
   421→| CraftQueueItem pool (5 items) | ~780 B | Static |
   422→| ActiveMeteors pointer array | 2 KB | Static |
   423→| Peak Meteor objects (up to 500) | up to ~36 KB | Heap (dynamic) |
   424→| WiFiManager + HTTP overhead | ~15-25 KB | Heap |
   425→| TinyXML2 parse tree (temporary) | ~5-15 KB | Heap (during parse) |
   426→| **Total peak estimate** | **~107-130 KB** | |
   427→
   428→ESP32 has ~320 KB SRAM total, with IDF overhead consuming ~100-130 KB. This leaves ~190-220 KB available. At peak meteor count, the system operates with **~60-110 KB of free heap** — workable but with limited margin, especially given heap fragmentation from `new`/`delete` Meteor churn.
   429→
   430→### LED Rendering Performance
   431→
   432→`FastLED.show()` at `main.cpp:2025` uses the WS2812B protocol across all 4 strips. With ESP32 RMT outputting in parallel, the blocking time equals the longest strip:
   433→
   434→```
   435→960 LEDs * 24 bits * 1.25us/bit = ~28.8ms (inner ring)
   436→```
   437→
   438→This gives a hard ceiling of **~34 FPS maximum**. The target of 60 FPS (`fpsRate = 60` at line 352) is unachievable. The `fpsInMs = 1000 / fpsRate` value computed at line 531 is **never used as a frame limiter** — `FastLED.show()` is called unconditionally on every loop iteration.
   439→
   440→### Critical Performance Issues
   441→
   442→#### P1. Meteor Heap Fragmentation — HIGH
   443→
   444→Each animation cycle creates multiple `Meteor` objects via `new` (`main.cpp:1241`) and deletes them via `delete` (`main.cpp:1903`). With up to 500 slots and animations repeating every ~3 seconds, this creates continuous heap fragmentation. Over hours/days of runtime, this can lead to allocation failures.
   445→
   446→**Fix:** Implement a fixed-size Meteor pool allocator.
   447→
   448→#### P2. LittleFS Double Write-Read Per Data Cycle — HIGH
   449→
   450→In `fetchHTTPData()`, the HTTP response is written to `/temp.xml` on LittleFS, then immediately read back into `xmlDataBuffer` in `fetchData()`. The `String res` already holds the data in RAM. This doubles I/O per cycle and accumulates flash wear (~8,640 write/delete cycles per day).
   451→
   452→**Fix:** Pass the HTTP response string directly to `parseData()` instead of routing through the filesystem.
   453→
   454→#### P3. No Frame Rate Limiter — HIGH
   455→
   456→`updateAnimation()` is called on every `loop()` iteration with no delay or frame-rate gate. `FastLED.show()` is called unconditionally, transmitting all pixel data even when nothing visually meaningful has changed since the last frame. This wastes CPU and could be capped at the achievable ~30 FPS.
   457→
   458→**Fix:** Add `EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(33)` around the render path, and `vTaskDelay(1)` when skipping frames.
   459→
   460→#### P4. `DevUtils::termColor()` Uses `std::map` with Heap Allocation — HIGH
   461→
   462→`DevUtils.cpp:4-55` uses a `static std::map<std::string, const char*>` for ANSI escape code lookup. Every call constructs a temporary `std::string` on the heap for the key lookup. This runs dozens of times per parse cycle when serial output is enabled.
   463→
   464→**Fix:** Replace with a simple switch statement or lookup array returning `const char*`.
   465→
   466→#### P5. Semaphore Held for ~1 Second During Parse — MEDIUM
   467→
   468→`parseData()` holds `freeListMutex` for the entire parse duration (~900-1000ms including `vTaskDelay(100)` calls at each loop iteration). `freeSemaphoreItem()` on Core 1 waits only 500ms. If the mutex is held longer, item return fails silently.
   469→
   470→**Fix:** Reduce critical section scope — only hold the mutex during pool allocation/deallocation, not during the full parse.
   471→
   472→#### P6. WiFi Always-On Dual Mode — MEDIUM
   473→
   474→WiFi runs in `WIFI_AP_STA` mode permanently, keeping both station and soft AP active. The AP consumes ~50-100mA continuously even when no clients are connected.
   475→
   476→**Fix:** After initial configuration, switch to `WIFI_STA` mode.
   477→
   478→#### P7. Boot Time: ~15-20 Seconds — MEDIUM
   479→
   480→Two `delay(1000)` calls contribute 2 seconds; WiFi connection takes 3-10 seconds; SpacecraftData unconditionally writes all 3 JSON files to flash on every boot (even though the data is hardcoded and cannot change between boots). Adding a version check could skip the writes on normal boots.
   481→
   482→#### P8. Double Pass Over 500-Slot Meteor Array Per Frame — MEDIUM
   483→
   484→Every frame iterates the full `ActiveMeteors[500]` array twice: once in `drawMeteors()` and once in `updateMeteors()`. When only 10 meteors are active, 98% of iterations are null-pointer checks. A packed array with an active count would eliminate this waste.
   485→
   486→#### P9. XML Parse Traversal Overhead — MEDIUM
   487→
   488→The counter-based position tracking system (`stationCount`, `dishCount`, `targetCount`) requires iterating through the full DOM to reach the desired position on each parse cycle. The outer loop at line 2396 (`for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)`) runs the entire parse logic twice as a retry, doubling parse time.
   489→
   490→#### P10. `logOutput()` Uses `malloc` Per Call — LOW
   491→
   492→The debug function allocates a dynamic buffer via `malloc` on every invocation. A fixed-size stack buffer would eliminate heap allocation in the logging path.
   493→
   494→---
   495→

  1089→uint8_t regionWrap(int8_t region, bool isDown)
  1090→{
  1091→	if (isDown) {
  1092→		if (region == outerChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1093→		if (region == outerChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1094→		if (region < 0) return outerChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1095→	} else {
  1096→		if (region == middleChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1097→		if (region == middleChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1098→		if (region < 0) return middleChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1099→	}
  1100→
  1101→	return region;
  1102→}

### 4. **Reference "S7" in codebase-analysis.md**

**Located at:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/docs/codebase-analysis.md:359-365`

### **S7. Unpinned Dependency Versions (Supply Chain Risk) — MEDIUM**

```
Location: platformio.ini:29-30

WiFiManager and tinyxml2 are pulled from git HEAD without version 
pinning. A supply chain attack or breaking change would be pulled 
automatically.

Fix: Pin to specific commit hashes or tagged releases.
```

**Analysis Context:**
- This is a **medium-severity security finding** in the comprehensive codebase analysis
- Identified in the "Short-Term — Next Sprint (1-2 Weeks)" remediation roadmap as item #14
- The issue has already been discovered and documented by the project's code review process

---

### 5. **Dependency Pinning Strategy Summary**

| Approach | Libraries | Risk Level | Status |
|----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| **Caret-Pinned** | ArduinoJson, FastLED | Low-Medium | Safe: minor/patch updates only |
| **Unpinned (HEAD)** | WiFiManager, tinyxml2 | **High** | ⚠️ Vulnerable to breaking changes |

**Key Findings:**

1. **ArduinoJson & FastLED:** Using caret versioning (`^X.Y.Z`) provides reasonable protection by allowing only patch-level changes within a minor version
2. **WiFiManager & tinyxml2:** Pulling directly from git HEAD creates supply chain risk:
   - No protection against breaking API changes
   - No protection against malicious commits
   - Builds are non-deterministic across time
   - Previous attempt to pin to `^2.0.15-rc.1` was abandoned (line 28 is commented out)

---

### 6. **Recommendations for Dependency Management**

Based on the S7 finding and best practices:

1. **Immediate:** Pin WiFiManager to a specific tag or commit hash
   - Current version installed is 2.0.17 — pin to this or latest stable
   - Example: `https://github.com/tzapu/WiFiManager.git@2.0.17`

2. **Immediate:** Pin tinyxml2 to a specific commit

   - Example: `https://github.com/leethomason/tinyxml2.git@<commit-hash>`

3. **Recommended:** Use semantic versioning for all git-based dependencies where tags exist

## JPL-MiniPulse Captive Portal & Web Server Code Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete findings:

---

### 1. **HTML Templates & Embedded HTML Strings**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3330-3362

Only **one custom HTML template** is embedded in the codebase:

```cpp
const char* update_button_html = R"---(
    <div>
        <div style="display: inline-block; border: 1px solid gray;padding:5px 20px;">
            <p id="firmwareStatus" style="margin-top:0;></p>
            <p id="updateResponse"></p>
            <button id="updateButton">Update Firmware</button>
        </div>
    </div>
    <script>
        fetch('/get-latest-version-number')
        .then(function (response) {
            return response.text();
        }).
        then(function (text) {
            document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").innerHTML = text;
            console.log(text);
        })

        document.getElementById("updateButton").addEventListener('click', function() {
            fetch('/trigger-firmware-update')
            .then(function (response) {
                return response.text();
            })
            .then(function (text) {
                document.getElementById("updateResponse").innerHTML = text;
                console.log("response:", text);
            })
            .catch(function (error) {
                console.error(error);
            });
        });
    </script>
)---";
```

This is injected into the WiFi portal as a custom head element via:
```cpp
wm.setCustomHeadElement(update_button_html);  // Line 3364
```

All other portal forms are **generated by WiFiManager library** (not custom HTML strings). The actual portal configuration form rendering is delegated to the WiFiManager library, which auto-generates HTML from the `WiFiManagerParameter` objects defined at lines 3310-3327.

---

### 2. **Web Server Route Handlers (Accepting User Input)**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 831-861 (webServerCallback function)

Three HTTP endpoints are registered:

#### **A. `/get-remote-version-number` (HTTP_GET)**
```cpp
wm.server->on("/get-remote-version-number", HTTP_GET, []() {
    const char* remoteFirmwareVersion = getRemoteFirmwareVersion();
    String response = "Remote Version: " + String(remoteFirmwareVersion);
    wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", response);
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters)
- **Action:** Fetches remote firmware version from `develop.kellerdigital.com`

#### **B. `/get-latest-version-number` (HTTP_GET)**
```cpp
wm.server->on("/get-latest-version-number", HTTP_GET, []() {
    const char* remoteFirmwareVersion = getRemoteFirmwareVersion();
    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
    const char* updateAvailableText = updateAvailable ? "true" : "false";
    String response = "Current version: " + String(currentFirmwareVersion) + 
                      "<br>Remote Version: " + String(remoteFirmwareVersion) + 
                      "<br>Update available: " + String(updateAvailableText);
    wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", response);
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters)
- **Action:** Returns version comparison info

#### **C. `/trigger-firmware-update` (HTTP_GET)** ⚠️ CRITICAL
```cpp
wm.server->on("/trigger-firmware-update", HTTP_GET, []() {
    bool updateAvailable = checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable();
    updateFirmwareOta();  // Initiates OTA update
    if (updateAvailable) {
        wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", "New firmware available, updating...");
    } else {
        wm.server->send(200, "text/plain", "Firmware is up to date");
    }
});
```
- **Input:** None (no parameters or body)
- **Action:** **Triggers firmware update immediately** with NO authentication
- **Vulnerability:** S2 (Unauthenticated OTA Trigger) — combined with S1 allows full device compromise

---

### **Portal Form Parameters (WiFiManager)**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3310-3327

Five configuration parameters are exposed via the WiFi portal:

| Parameter Name | Input Type | Min | Max | Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | range slider | 8 | 160 | `param_brightness` | Maps 0-100 → 8-160 |
| `force-dummy-data` | range slider | 8 | 160 | `param_force_dummy_data` | ⚠️ Uses same range as brightness (bug) |
| `show_serial` | number | 0 | 1 | `param_show_serial` | Boolean flag |
| `show_diagnostics` | number | 0 | 1 | `param_show_diagnostics` | Boolean flag |
| `force_animation_type` | number | 0 | 5 | `param_force_animation_type` | 6 animation types |

The portal form is handled by the `saveParamsCallback()` function (lines 938-1042).

### 3. **Input Validation Analysis**

**Location:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 938-1042 (saveParamsCallback)

**Critical Finding: NO SERVER-SIDE VALIDATION**

#### **Data Flow for Each Parameter:**

**A. Brightness (lines 995-1016)**
```cpp
String brightnessValue = getParam("brightness");          // Gets raw string
int brightnessInt = atoi(brightnessValue.c_str());        // ⚠️ atoi() - NO error checking
int brightnessMapped = MathHelpers::map(brightnessInt, 0, 100, 8, 160);
FileUtils::config.displayLED.brightness = brightnessInt;  // ⚠️ Stores unmapped value
FastLED.setBrightness(brightnessInt);                     // ⚠️ Uses unmapped value
```
- **Validation:** Client-side HTML `min='8' max='160'` ONLY
- **Issue:** `atoi()` returns 0 on parse failure (silent failure)
- **Issue:** The value is mapped but the unmapped value is stored in config
- **Issue:** Non-integer values silently convert to 0

**B. Show Serial (lines 943-960)**
```cpp
String showSerialValue = getParam("show_serial");
bool showSerialValueBool = strcmp(showSerialValue.c_str(), "1") == 0 ? true : false;
FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial = showSerialValueBool;
```
- **Validation:** String comparison to "1" (any other value = false)
- **Issue:** No validation that input is "0" or "1"

**C. Show Diagnostics (lines 965-980)**
```cpp
String showDiagnosticsValue = getParam("show_diagnostics");
bool showDiagnosticsValueBool = strcmp(showDiagnosticsValue.c_str(), "1") == 0 ? true : false;
FileUtils::config.debugUtils.diagMeasure = showDiagnosticsValueBool;
```
- **Validation:** Same as Show Serial (string comparison)
- **Issue:** No validation

**D. Force Animation Type (lines 985-991)**
```cpp
String forcedAnimationTypeValue = getParam("force_animation_type");
animate.forcedAnimationType = atoi(forcedAnimationTypeValue.c_str());
```
- **Validation:** Client-side HTML `min='0' max='5'` ONLY
- **Issue:** `atoi()` with no range validation (can exceed 5)
- **Issue:** No error checking if non-integer provided

**E. Force Dummy Data (lines 1021-1038)**
```cpp
String forceDummyDataInputValue = getParam("force_dummy_data");
int forceDummyDataInt = atoi(forceDummyDataInputValue.c_str());
FileUtils::config.wifiNetwork.forceDummyData = forceDummyDataInt;
```
- **Validation:** Client-side HTML `min='8' max='160'` ONLY
- **Issue:** Same `atoi()` issues as brightness
- **Bug:** This parameter uses brightness range instead of binary flag

---

### 4. **Reference S5 - Input Validation Weaknesses**

From `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/docs/codebase-analysis.md`, lines 341-347:

**S5. Input Validation Weaknesses on Portal Parameters**

> Portal values are converted via `atoi()` with no range validation before being applied to config.

Specific lines cited:
- **Line 995:** `int brightnessInt = atoi(brightnessValue.c_str());`
- **Line 1005:** (unmapped brightness stored)
- **Line 1030:** `int forceDummyDataInt = atoi(forceDummyDataInputValue.c_str());`

**Recommended Fix:**
> Use `strtol()` with error checking and clamp values server-side.

**Additional Context:** The analysis document also references that this is combined with **S4 (No CSRF Protection)** — any client on the network can forge configuration changes without authentication tokens.

---

### 5. **Reference S10 - innerHTML Usage**

From `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/docs/codebase-analysis.md`, lines 383-389:

**S10. XSS via innerHTML in Portal JavaScript**

Two instances found in the custom HTML template (lines 3344 and 3354):

```javascript
// Line 3344: Firmware status display
document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").innerHTML = text;

// Line 3354: Update response display  
document.getElementById("updateResponse").innerHTML = text;
```

**Security Issue:**
> Custom portal HTML uses `innerHTML` to render server responses directly into the DOM. A MITM attacker on the HTTP firmware endpoint could inject JavaScript.

**Attack Vector:**
1. Device fetches version from `http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/latest_version.txt` (plain HTTP)
2. MITM attacker intercepts response
3. Attacker injects HTML/JavaScript payload
4. Browser executes injected code in portal context

**Recommended Fix:**
> Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`

**Corrected Code Should Be:**
```javascript
document.getElementById("firmwareStatus").textContent = text;
document.getElementById("updateResponse").textContent = text;
```

---

### **Summary of Findings**

| Item | Location | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| **HTML Templates** | `src/main.cpp:3330-3362` | 1 custom template for firmware update button |
| **Route Handlers** | `src/main.cpp:831-861` | 3 endpoints: 2 read-only, 1 write (unauthenticated) |
| **Portal Forms** | `src/main.cpp:3310-3327` | 5 parameters via WiFiManager |
| **Form Processing** | `src/main.cpp:938-1042` | saveParamsCallback() |
| **Input Validation** | Throughout saveParamsCallback() | **NONE at server-side** |
| **S5 Reference** | codebase-analysis.md:341-347 | atoi() without range validation |
| **S10 Reference** | codebase-analysis.md:383-389 | innerHTML at lines 3344, 3354 |

**Critical Security Issues:**
- No CSRF protection on form submissions
- No server-side input validation (atoi() silent failures)
- XSS vulnerability via innerHTML in firmware update template
- OTA endpoint triggers update with no authentication
- OTA downloads firmware over plain HTTP (S1)

     4→ * Converts a hue int (0-360 degrees) to a 16 bit int
     5→ * The NeoPixel HSV color value takes a 16bit int
     6→ * 
     7→ * @param degree The degree of the hue value
     8→ * @return A 16bit int for use in Adafruit_NeoPixel::ColorsHSV
     9→*/
    10→int MathHelpers::degreeToSixteenbit(int degree) {
    11→  // Max value of uint16_t is 65535
    12→  return (degree * 65535) / 360;
    13→}
    14→
    15→/**
    16→ * Custom exponent function
    17→ * The C++ pow() function is very slow, this should be quicker
    18→ * 
    19→ * @param float a The base, float between 0 and 1
    20→ * @param int b The Exponent
    21→ * @return Float result
    22→*/
    23→float MathHelpers::mPower(float a, int b) {
    24→  float result = a;
    25→  for (int i = 1; i < b; i++) {
    26→    result = result * a;
    27→  }
    28→  return result;
    29→}
    30→long MathHelpers::map(long x, long in_min, long in_max, long out_min, long out_max) {
    31→    const long run = in_max - in_min;
    32→    if(run == 0){
    33→        return -1; // AVR returns -1, SAM returns 0
    34→    }
    35→    const long rise = out_max - out_min;
    36→    const long delta = x - in_min;
    37→    return (delta * rise) / run + out_min;
    38→}

Three security items from `docs/ROADMAP-1.1.0.md` that harden the captive portal and build pipeline against supply-chain and XSS risks. All changes are in two files.

| WiFiManager | `https://github.com/tzapu/WiFiManager.git` | `https://github.com/tzapu/WiFiManager.git#v2.0.17` |
| tinyxml2 | `https://github.com/leethomason/tinyxml2` | `https://github.com/leethomason/tinyxml2#9.0.0` |

These match the currently installed versions. Remove the commented-out `^2.0.15-rc.1` lines as they're now superseded.

## Item 15 — Portal input validation (S5, MED)

**File:** `src/main.cpp`, `saveParamsCallback()` (lines 938–1042)

Replace raw `atoi()` calls with `strtol()` + range clamping for the three integer parameters:

| Parameter | Current | Clamp Range | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| `brightness` | `atoi()` at line 1000 | 8–160 | Matches HTML min/max on the slider |
| `force_animation_type` | `atoi()` at line 990 | 0–5 | Matches HTML min/max |
| `force_dummy_data` | `atoi()` at line 1025 | 0–1 | This is a boolean flag; clamp to 0 or 1 |

**Approach for each:** Replace `atoi(x.c_str())` with an inline `strtol` + clamp pattern:

\```cpp
long raw = strtol(value.c_str(), nullptr, 10);
int clamped = (raw < MIN) ? MIN : (raw > MAX) ? MAX : (int)raw;
\```

The two boolean parameters (`show_serial`, `show_diagnostics`) already use `strcmp` to "1" which is safe — no changes needed.
